headline: You're not in trouble. Asking for help is brave.
subline: If something feels wrong, you can talk to someone right now.

helplines.name: Childline
helplines.desc: For any child who needs help. Free, any time, day or night.

helplines.name: Emergency
helplines.desc: If you or someone else is in danger right now.

helplines.name: Free Legal Aid (NALSA)
helplines.desc: Free help from lawyers. Children get legal aid for free.

helplines.name: Cyber Crime Helpline
helplines.desc: If someone is bullying, threatening or tricking you online.

tellAnAdult.title: How to tell a trusted adult
steps: Pick someone you trust: a parent, teacher, school counsellor, Anganwadi didi or a relative.
Find a quiet moment when they can listen.
Say it simply: "Something happened that made me feel unsafe. I need help."
If they don't listen, tell another adult. Keep telling until someone helps.

yourRights.title: Your rights when you ask for help
points: Your name and identity must be kept secret.
You can talk where you feel comfortable, with a parent or trusted person next to you.
Children can get a lawyer for free.

items.name: NCPCR
items.desc: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights. Takes complaints about any child rights problem, including online through its e-Baal Nidan portal.

items.name: Child Welfare Committee (CWC)
items.desc: Every district has one. It protects children who need care and safety.

items.name: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA)
items.desc: Gives free legal help in your district.

disclaimer: Saksham is a learning app. It does not contact anyone for you. In an emergency, call 112.
